chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Ibn Ri'ab, from Abu 'Ubayda, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: Whoever issues fatwas to the people without knowledge and without guidance from God — the Angels of Mercy and the Angels of Punishment curse him, and the burden of sin of those who acted by his fatwa attaches to him.

key_terms.أَفْتَى: afta — to issue a fatwa (religious ruling); the authority to issue fatwas is restricted to those possessing proper knowledge
key_terms.مَلَائِكَةُ الرَّحْمَةِ وَالْعَذَابِ: Angels of Mercy and Punishment — both categories of angels united in cursing the unauthorized mufti, emphasizing the gravity of the sin
key_terms.هُدًى مِنَ اللَّهِ: guidance from God — indicating that legitimate religious rulings must derive from divine revelation, not personal opinion
key_terms.وِزْرُ: wizr — burden, sin, responsibility; the issuer bears the accumulated sins of all who followed his errant ruling

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir say about issuing fatwas without knowledge?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) issues a severe warning against issuing religious rulings (fatwas) without proper knowledge and divine guidance. This hadith was addressed in a context where unauthorized persons presumed to issue religious verdicts during the early Islamic period, misleading the community. The Imam emphasizes that such a person bears not only their own sin but the accumulated sins of all who follow their errant rulings — making unauthorized fatwa-issuance among the gravest violations of religious responsibility.
